Project page: Introduction sec:intro Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models pretrained on large-scale datasets demonstrate remarkable semantic generalization, seamlessly interpreting novel instructions and adapting to diverse tasks~ black2024pi0, intelligence2025pi_, bjorck2025gr00t . However, this semantic capability often masks a severe kinematic fragility: even minor out-of-distribution (OOD) visual shifts, such as an altered camera angle, a novel background texture, or changed lighting, can cause catastrophic execution failures~ fei2025libero, zhou2510libero, wang2025vlatest . Under these conditions, the underlying task semantics remain identical, yet the policy's action generation diverges wildly from safe trajectories. This reveals a critical bottleneck for real-world deployment: while pretrained VLAs know what to achieve, their over-reliance on perturbation-sensitive visual features causes them to easily lose track of how to physically execute the task. A natural approach to improving robustness is to finetune pretrained policies with augmented datasets that explicitly expose the models to perturbed conditions~ xu2026apt, guo2026robustness . However, exhaustively curating data and finetuning across the infinite long-tail of real-world environmental variations is both costly and practically impossible. Meanwhile, recent test-time scaling methods attempt to improve robustness without modifying model parameters by emphasizing task-relevant visual cues~ hancock2025run, zhang2026probeact , adapting via in-context information~ jang2026ravla, sridhar2025ricl , or steering action generation away from undesirable behaviors~ liu2026vls, nguyen2026sdn . While these approaches help mitigate the influence of visual noise or steer policies away from failure states, they fundamentally ignore a powerful asset: the policy's own successful training experience. The precise motion patterns, spatial relationships, and temporal transitions required to solve the task are already embedded in the training demonstrations. The challenge is that contextual perturbations obscure the correspondence between the current OOD observation and these learned motion primitives, preventing the policy from reusing its own prior successes. Retrieval offers a natural mechanism to recall this prior experience, but applying flat retrieval to robotic trajectories is notoriously difficult. Prior robot-learning methods often retrieve demonstrations based on affordance similarity~ kuang2024ram , motion correspondence~ lin2024flowretrieval , or trajectory conditioning~ park2026retrieve . However, demonstrations are not isolated visual snapshots; they are highly structured spatiotemporal executions~ xu2026stellavla . Standard retrieval methods that match visual embeddings fail to capture this sequential geometry, conflating two distinct problems: where does the current execution lie within the trajectory space, and what specific motion primitive should follow? To recover from an OOD-induced error, a retrieval mechanism must dynamically align the robot's ongoing geometric context with the underlying structure of prior demonstrations, entirely independent of visual noise. To bridge this gap, we introduce R2A (Retrieve to Act), a test-time scaling framework that formulates OOD robustness purely as a geometric experience retrieval problem. R2A bypasses fragile visual features by organizing successful training demonstrations into an offline motion primitive graph. Nodes encode the pure kinematic geometry of past executions (poses, states, and frame-wise changes), while edges capture the spatiotemporal transitions across and within tasks. At the onset of an episode, a diffusion-based rectification module first projects any out-of-distribution initial robot states back into the established training manifold. During continuous execution, R2A then utilizes a query-dependent Graph Neural Network (GNN) to dynamically propagate the VLA's current kinematic trajectory through the graph. This explicitly localizes the robot's current progress and retrieves the most structurally compatible future motion primitives. A learned harmonization module then adaptively weight-fuses this retrieved geometric prior with the VLA's predicted actions. By doing so, R2A seamlessly rectifies erroneous trajectories caused by visual OOD shifts, restoring successful motion patterns without altering the frozen VLA parameters. We evaluate R2A across three diverse VLA architectures, including GR00T N1.7~ bjorck2025gr00t , ~ intelligence2025pi_ , and StableVLA~ fu2026stablevla , under seven types of systematic perturbations in LIBERO-Plus~ fei2025libero . R2A consistently improves the robustness of all three policies, achieving gains of up to in success rate. We further evaluate on the challenging RoboTwin2.0-Plus benchmark~ zhang2026world where R2A improves the success rate from to . On a real-world task with Aloha embodiment, R2A similarly achieves up to a improvement in success rate over the corresponding base policies, demonstrating substantial gains in physical deployment. Related Work Test-Time Robustness of VLA Policies. Finetuning pretrained policies across the infinite long-tail of real-world environmental shifts is costly and practically impossible. Test-time scaling provides an efficient alternative, primarily by emphasizing task-relevant visual features or suppressing spurious cues at inference time. For instance, BYOVLA~ hancock2025run suppresses irrelevant regions via image inpainting, VLS~ liu2026vls relies on external vision models to generate steering rewards, and SDN~ nguyen2026sdn steers action generation away from OOD-induced negative behaviors. ProbeAct~ zhang2026probeact leverages 3D positional tracking to detect and recover from grasping failures. Despite their effectiveness, these methods often require costly external visual modules~ nguyen2026sdn, hancock2025run, liu2026vls and over-rely on test-time visual cues, neglecting the rich behavioral priors already embedded in the training data. R2A overcomes this by structuring prior experience into a spatiotemporal motion primitive graph, bypassing fragile visual features entirely to dynamically retrieve and reinstate geometrically aligned behaviors. Retrieval-Augmented Robot Learning. Recent works demonstrate that useful experience need not be compressed entirely into policy parameters. Methods like RAM~ kuang2024ram construct reusable affordance memories, while Retrieve, Don't Retrain~ park2026retrieve conditions frozen policies on retrieved trajectories to avoid per-task finetuning. Other approaches emphasize low-level behavioral correspondence or action-sequence similarity to recover shared structures across visual variations~ lin2024flowretrieval, lee2025class . While these works establish the value of external experience, they predominantly treat retrieval as a static matching problem between independent observations. Demonstrations, however, are highly structured temporal executions. R2A differentiates itself by treating the retrieval query not as an isolated snapshot, but as an ongoing geometric execution. By mapping the robot's current trajectory into a structured graph of successful rollouts, R2A first dynamically localizes the execution state, and subsequently retrieves a structurally compatible future continuation. Graph-Structured and Relational Retrieval. Graph-enhanced retrieval leverages structural dependencies to improve evidence selection, commonly using query-conditioned GNNs in semantic domains~ luo2025gfmrag . While recent robotics methods incorporate motion, they differ significantly in mechanism and scope. FlowRetrieval~ lin2024flowretrieval maps visual optical flow into a latent space for few-shot image retrieval, leaving it vulnerable to visual OOD shifts. CLASS~ lee2025class uses motion similarity strictly as a pretraining contrastive loss rather than for test-time retrieval. ReGIL~ zhang2026regil uses motion to generate auxiliary rewards for local trajectory alignment, but still fundamentally depends on standard, visually-driven retrieval pipelines. R2A diverges by using motion to construct an explicit topological graph of pure kinematic states, completely decoupled from fragile visual pixels. Rather than using motion for representation learning, visual flow matching, or auxiliary rewards, R2A deploys a query-conditioned GNN over this geometric graph to perform dynamic execution localization. This explicitly spatial retrieval mechanism continuously infers the robot's ongoing position within prior structured successes, enabling robust retrieval of future geometric trajectories even under severe visual perturbations. Method sec:method Preliminaries Problem Formulation sec:preliminary At control step , the robot's kinematic state comprises joint angles , the forward-kinematic end-effector pose , and a binary gripper state . Conditioned on visual observations and a language instruction , a frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policy generates an action chunk every steps. We decouple this prediction into continuous spatial pose commands and discrete gripper commands . While generalizes well in-distribution, it remains highly sensitive to visual OOD shifts (e.g., altered viewpoints or lighting). These perturbations corrupt the visual observation space, frequently causing the spatial predictions to diverge from safe, successful trajectories. To resolve this, we formulate OOD recovery as a visual-feature-free, geometry-grounded retrieval problem, dynamically correcting using historical motion primitives from the training corpus. R2A Overview To explicitly leverage prior training experience, we introduce Retrieve to Act (R2A). Given a set of successful training demonstrations , we first construct an offline motion primitive graph , where nodes encode the kinematics of demonstration segments (poses, states, and frame-wise changes) and edges capture spatiotemporal geometry. title: GeoGSplat: Geometry-Grounded Non-Pixel-Aligned Gaussian Splatting
summary: Feed-forward Gaussian Splatting enables efficient novel view synthesis, but pixel-aligned prediction makes the primitive count grow with image resolution and view count, leading to substantial redundancy and increased computational cost. Non-pixel-aligned methods address this limitation by predicting a fixed number of Gaussians. Without explicit ray and depth constraints, these methods yield misplaced Gaussian centers, causing rendering artifacts under large viewpoint changes. To address this issue, we introduce GeoGSplat, a geometry-grounded feed-forward model that explicitly incorporates geometric priors into the non-pixel-aligned framework. A dual-branch encoder constructs Anchors and Triplane to capture coarse 3D structure and fine-grained scene features, respectively. Subsequently, a hierarchical decoder progressively decodes dense 3D points and Gaussian primitives, enabling 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis. GeoGSplat surpasses both state-of-the-art pixel-aligned and non-pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting methods on DTU and NRGBD in terms of novel view synthesis and reconstruction. The advantage of our geometry-grounded paradigm further increases as target viewpoints move farther from the input cameras, demonstrating stronger generalization to large viewpoint changes. Project Page: https://comedy0913.github.io/projects/geogsplat

Page: Introduction Feed-forward Gaussian Splatting~ charatan2024pixelsplat,chen2024mvsplat,zhang2024gs,tokengs2026 aims to directly predict Gaussian primitives from a set of images, supporting novel view synthesis (NVS) and avoiding expensive per-scene optimization~ kerbl20233d . Most existing methods~ charatan2024pixelsplat,chen2024mvsplat conduct pixel-aligned predictions, where each input pixel is associated with a predicted Gaussian primitive. Such methods inherit explicit geometric constraints from per-pixel depth prediction, which restricts Gaussian centers to a geometrically meaningful 3D surface and thus reduces the ambiguity of appearance learning during rasterization. However, this paradigm couples Gaussian primitives to both image resolution and the number of input views, resulting in considerable computational overhead. As illustrated in Fig.~ fig:Comparison , the number of predicted primitives grows rapidly with the number of input views. Moreover, overlapping regions across images produce multiple Gaussians for the same scene content, introducing substantial redundancy. Some recent methods~ tokengs2026,li2026locusgs,li2026querysplat , adopt a non-pixel-aligned paradigm that predicts a fixed number of Gaussians. These methods typically decode Gaussians from a set of learnable tokens that aggregate multi-view image features through attention. While this formulation removes the scaling dependency of pixel-aligned prediction, it also discards the geometric constraints provided by per-pixel depth. Primitives are learned from photometric supervision, leaving the Gaussian centers underconstrained and resulting in inaccurate geometry and overfitting to the observed viewpoints. Such Gaussians may produce plausible renderings near the input cameras, but they tend to yield strong rendering artifacts under larger viewpoint changes. To address this limitation, we introduce GeoGSplat, a geometry-grounded non-pixel-aligned framework consisting of a dual-branch structured encoder and a geometry-guided hierarchical decoder. The encoder captures complementary scene properties through Anchors and Triplane. Anchors comprise sparse 3D spheres with learnable centers and adaptive radii, providing coarse geometric constraints on the scene structure. Triplane comprises three orthogonal 2D feature maps that encode fine-grained high-dimensional scene features queryable at arbitrary 3D coordinates. Building on the two complementary representations, the decoder progressively converts sparse geometric priors into dense 3D points and Gaussian primitives. We first perform Anchor-to-Point decoding by sampling Triplane features within each Anchor region to predict a set of dense 3D points. We then apply Point-to-Gaussian decoding, re-querying the Triplane at the decoded 3D points to predict corresponding Gaussian primitives. This hierarchical design establishes interaction between Anchors and Triplane, using Anchor geometry to constrain point reconstruction and employing fine-grained Triplane features to enable geometric refinement and appearance learning. We conduct experiments on DTU~ jensen2014large and NRGBD~ azinovic2022neural for object-level and scene-level evaluations, respectively. Our GeoGSplat outperforms both non-pixel-aligned and pixel-aligned competitors on these datasets in terms of NVS and 3D reconstruction. Furthermore, we evaluate GeoGSplat under a challenging setting by progressively moving the target cameras farther from the input cameras. Its performance advantage becomes increasingly pronounced under larger viewpoint changes, showing stronger robustness and generalization under large viewpoint changes enabled by our geometric priors. Our contributions are summarized below. We introduce a geometry-grounded non-pixel-aligned paradigm for feed-forward Gaussian Splatting that incorporates explicit geometric priors, enabling high-quality NVS and 3D reconstruction in an efficient manner. We propose a dual-branch structured encoder that constructs Anchors and Triplane to capture complementary coarse 3D structure and fine-grained high-dimensional scene features, respectively. We develop a geometry-guided hierarchical decoder that progressively decodes dense 3D points and Gaussian primitives by querying Triplane features under Anchor-based geometric constraints. Related Works Pixel-aligned feed-forward Gaussian Splatting. Significant progress has been made in feed-forward Gaussian Splatting~ charatan2024pixelsplat,chen2024mvsplat,zhang2024gs,tokengs2026,szymanowicz2024splatter , predicting Gaussian primitives from images without per-scene optimization. Most existing approaches follow a pixel-aligned mechanism~ chen2024mvsplat,xu2025depthsplat,charatan2024pixelsplat , predicting a Gaussian primitive for each image pixel. Such predictions benefit from explicit geometric constraints imposed by the corresponding camera rays and per-pixel depths, which restrict Gaussian centers to plausible 3D locations. However, the pixel-aligned pipeline ties the number of Gaussians to the input image resolution and the number of views, leading to considerable redundancy and computational cost. Non-pixel-aligned models. Non-pixel-aligned methods remove correspondences between image pixels and Gaussian primitives, instead predicting Gaussians from aggregated image features or scene representations~ wang2026volsplat,zhang2026anchorsplat,li2026locusgs,tokengs2026,zhao2026rayzer,moreau2026off,li2026querysplat . However, removing pixel-to-Gaussian correspondences also eliminates the geometric constraints provided by per-pixel ray and depth. In this context, Gaussian centers tend to be inaccurately placed, leading to suboptimal solutions that overfit the observed viewpoints. While these primitives may still produce plausible renderings for novel views close to the input cameras, their geometric errors become increasingly exposed under large viewpoint changes, resulting in strong rendering artifacts. To tackle this issue, we introduce a new non-pixel-aligned paradigm that injects explicit geometric priors, enabling more robust NVS. Scene Representations. Existing feed-forward methods adopt various scene representations~ yao2018mvsnet,gu2020cascade,yu2021pixelnerf,wang2021ibrnet,chen2021mvsnerf,jiang2025rayzer,johari2022geonerf,wang2024dust3r,leroy2024grounding,wang2025vggt,xiang2026native . These representations play a critical role in Gaussian prediction. For instance, voxels and anchors constrain the spatial locations at which primitives are predicted~ lu2024scaffold,fridovich2022plenoxels ; Triplane~ hong2024lrm,zhang2024gs,chan2022efficient provides structured representations, where fine-grained high-dimensional scene features can be encoded and queried. Motivated by the complementarity of these two representations, GeoGSplat combines Anchors and Triplane, using Anchors to provide coarse geometric constraints and Triplane to supply fine-grained scene features. title: KEPT: Conformal Keepouts Kept in Planning for Enclosed-Space Navigation in Degraded Sensing
summary: Autonomous vehicles in enclosed spaces such as tunnels and mines rely on range maps that smoke, dust and fog make inaccurate. Conformal prediction calibrates a keepout around the mapped walls that covers the true unsafe set at a chosen probability. Typically an unmodified planner treats the keepout as an inflated obstacle, and nothing ensures that the vehicle can stop before the keepout as it moves when sensing degrades. In narrow passages this margin and the planner's buffer close the route, and existing remedies recover reach by relaxing the coverage level. This paper conditions the conformal margin on a label-free severity estimate to hold coverage near its target as degradation varies. A planning and control layer enforces one braking-distance condition on the keepout at plan time and at every command, takes the measured tracking residual as its only margin and never alters the keepout. The keepout is validated on ground-robot smoke recordings and the closed loop in simulated quadrotor flights in a foggy tunnel against the standard deployment. In closed-loop simulation the proposed system substantially reduces entries into the calibrated keepout and reaches numerically more goals than the deployment pattern in both calibration regimes, an observed gain of 3.2 percentage points pooled whose per-regime confidence intervals include zero. The per-class keepout holds its coverage near the target on held-out recordings.
full_text: Autonomous vehicles in enclosed spaces such as tunnels and mines rely on range maps that smoke, dust and fog make inaccurate. Conformal prediction calibrates a keepout around the mapped walls that covers the true unsafe set at a chosen probability. Typically an unmodified planner treats the keepout as an inflated obstacle, and nothing ensures that the vehicle can stop before the keepout as it moves when sensing degrades. In narrow passages this margin and the planner's buffer close the route, and existing remedies recover reach by relaxing the coverage level. This paper conditions the conformal margin on a label-free severity estimate to hold coverage near its target as degradation varies. A planning and control layer enforces one braking-distance condition on the keepout at plan time and at every command, takes the measured tracking residual as its only margin and never alters the keepout. The keepout is validated on ground-robot smoke recordings and the closed loop in simulated quadrotor flights in a foggy tunnel against the standard deployment. In closed-loop simulation the proposed system substantially reduces entries into the calibrated keepout and reaches numerically more goals than the deployment pattern in both calibration regimes, an observed gain of 3.2 percentage points pooled whose per-regime confidence intervals include zero. The per-class keepout holds its coverage near the target on held-out recordings. Planning under Uncertainty, Robot Safety, Collision Avoidance Introduction sec:intro Autonomous vehicles in tunnels, mines and collapsed structures navigate narrow passages on range maps that smoke, dust and fog make inaccurate~ tranzatto2022cerberus,zhao2024subtmrs,rasshofer2011weather . Conformal prediction calibrates a keepout around the mapped walls that covers each point of the true unsafe set at a chosen probability without a noise model~ vovk2005alrw,angelopoulos2023gentle . This coverage concerns the map, whereas staying out of the keepout and reaching the goal depend on planning and control. In the usual deployment the planner treats the conformal set as an obstacle~ lindemann2023safe,dixit2024pwc,sundarsingh2026semantic and keeps its own clearance buffer and collision check~ zhou2019fastplanner,zhou2021ego . In a narrow passage the buffer can close routes the keepout leaves open, and neither safeguard budgets the braking distance to a keepout that grows as degradation reveals walls late. Remedies lower the confidence level until a plan exists~ sundarsingh2026semantic,stamouli2024recursive or soften the constraint into a cost~ shin2026fcpmpc,guo2026coconav , giving up coverage or compliance. Conformal barrier filters act only at the command~ yang2023safe,dong2026risk , and plan-and-command checks target the motion of other agents~ guo2026coconav,suganda2026cert . Unlike these approaches, the proposed framework, KEPT (keepout enforcement in planning and tracking), leaves the keepout and its confidence level unchanged and enforces one braking-distance condition on it at plan time and at every command. Its components, conformal calibration, barrier functions and the planner, are established~ vovk2005alrw,ames2019cbf,zhou2019fastplanner , and the contributions lie in how the margin is conditioned, where the condition acts and what is measured. KEPT calibrates a one-sided bound on the LiDAR distance error and uses the resulting keepout in planning and in command filtering. By the robust-constraint argument of Lindemann et al.~ lindemann2023safe , adapted to perception error, an executed cell outside the keepout lies outside the true unsafe set whenever its perception error satisfies the calibrated bound. Statistical coverage at executed queries and the compliance of the vehicle set the scope of this implication and are treated separately. A keepout whose conformal margin is calibrated offline per severity class, and run-time margin selection, which picks the margin for each viewing direction and sweep from a label-free severity estimate. Coverage stays near target as fog varies around the vehicle and along the route, unlike a pooled margin~ dixit2024pwc or adaptive conformal inference~ gibbs2021aci,dixit2023adaptive , which needs online error feedback. Per-class validity is tested on ground-robot smoke recordings. The planning layer of KEPT, the planning and execution component that lets the framework use its calibrated keepout during navigation. It coordinates trajectory planning and command-level safety filtering by holding both to consistent constraints on the same certified keepout, which is never relaxed. The vehicle thereby enters the keepout in markedly fewer flights and reaches numerically more goals, a joint outcome obtained inside the certificate rather than by weakening it. A closed-loop evaluation of simulated quadrotor flights in which a keepout calibrated on real or simulated data is replayed identically for every stack, measuring executed keepout entries, reach and coverage on the same cells against the conformal deployment pattern and each enforcement point alone. Compliance improves substantially and observed pooled reach is numerically higher. Related Work sec:related Conformal prediction entered robot navigation as a way to bound the error of a predicted or sensed quantity before a planner consumes it. Lindemann et al. constrain a model predictive controller to avoid conformal regions around predicted agent trajectories, the robust-constraint argument that the clearance lemma of Section~ sec:problem -D adapts~ lindemann2023safe . Dixit et al. calibrate an occupancy inflation from one worst-case nonconformity score per calibration environment, the smallest inflation that covers the truth at every state of a fixed sampled set, and take one shared conformal threshold from the scores of all calibration environments~ dixit2024pwc . That construction supports planner-independent episode-level safety statements on new environments drawn as the calibration ones, given its stated assumptions. Sundarsingh et al. turn conformal label sets of a semantic map into class distances for a mission planner~ sundarsingh2026semantic , Sheng et al. adapt the conformal quantile on line inside partially observable planning in the presence of dynamic agents~ sheng2024pomdp , and Strawn et al. place a conformal predictor inside a safety filter for a learned controller~ strawn2023filter . In each, the region is an input to an otherwise unchanged planner or controller, and the braking distance of the vehicle to a region that moves as the map is revised is not part of the planning condition. When the inflated region closes a route, a second group recovers feasibility by changing the constraint. Sundarsingh et al. fall back to the largest confidence level at which a path exists~ sundarsingh2026semantic , Stamouli et al. relax the conformal constraints as new regions arrive to keep the controller recursively feasible~ stamouli2024recursive , Shin et al. offer a hard functional envelope or a soft penalty whose weight the user sets~ shin2026fcpmpc , and Guo et al. penalise the bound in the planner and verify the rollout afterwards~ guo2026coconav . Each buys feasibility by lowering the level or softening the constraint, and the set the vehicle respects is then not the calibrated one. A third group couples conformal regions to control barrier functions. Yang et al. derive a measurement-robust barrier from a conformal bound on the state estimate~ yang2023safe , and Dong et al. calibrate the inflation of obstacle ellipsoids from noisy point clouds and enforce it in a second-order cone layer~ dong2026risk . Both filter the command against a static set in simulation, neither acts at plan time, and Dong et al. note that their coverage and invariance results are not linked. A fourth group certifies trajectories at plan time and at run time without a conformal map certificate. FaSTrack plans in the sensed free space eroded by a worst-case tracking bound and tracks the plan by a least-restrictive controller~ chen2021fastrack , FASTER commits to a trajectory whose safe part ends in a stop inside known free space~ tordesillas2021faster , gatekeeper commits to backup trajectories that keep a safe set invariant~ agrawal2024gatekeeper , and CERT-Replan pairs a one-step barrier filter on adaptive conformal radii of moving obstacles and a horizon-level risk monitor that switches the planning mode~ suganda2026cert . Their safe sets are worst-case or adaptive to other agents, and none reports reach beside entries into a fixed statistical keepout on the same cells. Grid-distance barrier filters on quadrotors supply the filter mechanics adopted here~ ames2019cbf,raja2024ogmcbf,harms2025composite , and LiDAR models of fog inform the simulated degradation~ rasshofer2011weather,hahner2021fog , and neither line carries a certificate. Unlike these prior approaches, KEPT keeps one conformal keepout fixed for the whole planning stack and measures what the executed trajectory does relative to it, avoiding the relaxed confidence level and the softened constraint of the feasibility methods. Its planning layer enforces one braking-distance condition against the keepout in force at plan time and at the command, where CoCoNav uses its bound softly in the planner and CERT-Replan in the filter and monitor alone, and the plan-plus-verify structure receives a statistical keepout in place of a worst-case or agent-adaptive set. The planning layer takes the measured tracking residual as its only margin, and no second clearance term consumes the certified free space as in the deployment pattern. KEPT operates on a keepout whose margin is selected at run time per viewing direction from the sensing severity, which none of the conformal navigation methods above models. KEPT calibrates per cell and not per environment, a choice distinct from the severity conditioning, and the cell-level guarantee does not establish the planner-independent episode-level coverage that Dixit et al. obtain on their stated assumptions~ dixit2024pwc . KEPT is evaluated against the deployment pattern on the same cells and seeds, and its keepout entries, reach and certificate coverage are reported in one table, the measurement the barrier filters leave open. KEPT claims no trajectory-level probability guarantee, and the per-sample bound it inherits from the conformal statement is stated in Section~ sec:method beside its assumptions. Problem Statement and Certified Keepout sec:problem Setting and notation This section defines the certificate of KEPT. An autonomous vehicle moves in an enclosed workspace whose true obstacle set is . The distance to the nearest obstacle is , and the vehicle is modelled as a ball of radius around its centre. The true unsafe set of centre positions is therefore . The workspace is discretised into cubic cells of edge , every field below is evaluated at cell centres, denotes the cell that contains , and a cell is called unsafe when its centre lies in . The vehicle never observes . A mapping pipeline returns an estimate of the distance to the nearest surface, built from range sensing whose quality degrades along the route because of airborne obscurant, range-dependent dropout and surfaces seen at grazing angles. The estimation error is positive when a wall appears farther than it is, and this is the error that matters for safety. Table~ tab:notation collects the symbols of this section and the next. A keepout is a set of centre positions declared inadmissible, and the planner treats as its free space. The question of this section is how large must be for it to contain at a controlled rate, given only and a finite calibration record.
